title: Cosmic Potato Morphology — 3D Shape Inference, Null Models and Cross-Scale Universality
status: book-derived morphology hypothesis + quantitative 3D statistical model-selection programme
abstract: The Cosmic Potato hypothesis is scientifically meaningful only if 'potato-like' is defined before examining the target and tested against serious alternatives in three dimensions. Large-scale cosmic structures are not solid bodies: they are density/velocity fields, filaments, walls, nodes and attraction basins whose apparent boundaries depend on tracer selection, smoothing and reconstruction. This redevelopment therefore treats shape as a probabilistic inference problem. A frozen segmentation produces a 3D object or point process; descriptor vectors summarize axis ratios, Minkowski functionals, filamentarity, planarity, topology and roughness; uncertainty is propagated through the reconstruction; and candidate morphological families are compared with likelihood or simulation-based classification. A tuber model only gains evidence if it beats filament, wall, ellipsoid and cosmological-simulation nulls under the same pipeline and remains stable across reasonable viewing, masking and smoothing choices. Cross-scale universality is a second, harder hypothesis requiring a shared dimensionless descriptor distribution or generative scaling law across biological and cosmic objects. Visual resemblance alone carries almost no evidentiary weight.
research_question: Does a preregistered tuber-like 3D morphology class explain selected cosmic structures better than filamentary, sheet-like, ellipsoidal and simulation-derived alternatives, and is any resulting morphology genuinely scale-invariant across independent object classes?

object_definition.rule: Morphology is conditional on the object-definition pipeline; uncertainty in that pipeline must propagate into the shape claim.

descriptor_vector.topology: Use Betti numbers/Euler characteristic where the segmentation supports them.

probabilistic_classification.simulation_based: When analytic p(Z|M) is unavailable, estimate classifier/posterior calibration from forward simulations passed through the identical survey/segmentation pipeline.
probabilistic_classification.anti_overfit: Define the tuber class and priors using independent reference data, not the named target.

uncertainty_pipeline.bootstrap: Resample tracers where appropriate to estimate descriptor variance.
uncertainty_pipeline.reconstruction: Draw from distance/velocity-field posterior or catalog uncertainty model and rerun segmentation.
uncertainty_pipeline.mask: Apply the real survey mask to mocks rather than comparing ideal simulations with masked data.
uncertainty_pipeline.smoothing: Report descriptor trajectories Z(sigma_smooth) over a preregistered scale range instead of one favorable smoothing choice.
uncertainty_pipeline.output: p(Z|data,pipeline) rather than a single deterministic shape label.

orientation_and_projection.rotation_invariance: Intrinsic 3D descriptors should be invariant to coordinate rotation; projected 2D descriptors should be studied over lines of sight.
orientation_and_projection.projection_test: p(class_2D|view) quantifies how often non-tuber 3D structures appear tuber-like in projection.
orientation_and_projection.failure: A claim driven only by a favorable 2D projection is rejected as a 3D morphology result.

cross_scale_universality.null: Independent descriptor families by scale/object class.
cross_scale_universality.shared_model: A common dimensionless family or scaling law with limited class-specific parameters.
cross_scale_universality.comparison: Use out-of-sample predictive likelihood/Bayesian evidence/information criteria appropriate to the fitted hierarchy.
cross_scale_universality.stronger_test: A shared generative mechanism predicting multiple descriptors is substantially stronger than overlapping q,s ranges.

worked_test_protocol: Choose one target and freeze the 3D dataset/segmentation.
Predefine tuber and alternative morphology families on independent data/simulations.
Compute posterior distributions for Z including reconstruction/mask/smoothing uncertainty.
Pass all null simulations through the identical measurement pipeline.
Compare calibrated class probabilities or predictive scores.
Replicate on a second target before attempting cross-scale universality.
failure_conditions: Filament/skeleton/wall or generic simulation models predict the observed descriptors as well as or better than the tuber class.
Classification changes materially under reasonable segmentation, mask or smoothing choices.
The apparent tuber morphology exists only in selected 2D projections.
The tuber class was tuned after inspection of the target.
Cross-scale shared parameters fail to predict held-out biological/cosmic descriptor distributions.
boundary: A successful morphology classification would establish a useful geometric description, not a new cosmological force, universal potato ontology or causal mechanism by itself.
